<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/monitoring-plugin/pull/891):

>Some panels, like TraceTable and TracingGanttChart, utilize the RouterProvider to get a reference to the used router library of the host website (in this case, the OCP console).
>
>This PR configures the `<RouterProvider>` from Perses using the `react-router`.


Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/command-help?repo=openshift%2Fmonitoring-plugin).  If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin](https://github.com/openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin/issues/new) repository.
</details>

## Walkthrough The changes integrate router navigation capabilities into the PersesWrapper component by wrapping the Perses context tree with a RouterProvider from the plugin system, while introducing React Router integration through the useNavigate hook and Link component. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Router Provider Integration**
`web/src/components/dashboards/perses/PersesWrapper.tsx`|Wrapped Perses context tree with RouterProvider, added useNavigate hook and Router-related imports (Link, useNavigate from react-router; RouterProvider from `@perses-dev/plugin-system`), passed RouterComponent and navigate props to RouterProvider, maintained functional equivalence of conditional rendering logic.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 2 (Simple) | ⏱️ ~12 minutes
